title: Network Gateway Elevation: Graded Intake and Response Lanes for Private Deploys
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We receive frequent customer requests to 'elevate' or modify network gateway access for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments. These requests vary from low-risk IP allowlist updates to high-risk network topology changes (proxy bridges, NAT traversal, gateway firmware/upgrade windows) that impact air-gapped environments and upgrade safety. Currently intake is ad-hoc: tickets land in Support and are routed manually to Solutions or Eng with inconsistent scoring, leading to long SLAs, duplicated work, and occasional rollout regressions.

Goal: Design and ship a graded intake + response lanes system (self-serve, assisted, and escalation) that: 1) standardizes customer submissions for network changes, 2) produces a deterministic risk score and lane assignment, 3) provides playbooks and comms templates for each lane, and 4) integrates with PM/Eng triage dashboards and the Private Console so customers and internal teams have predictable timelines.

Scope: Non-bug customer requests related to networking, upgrades, and air-gapped constraints for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments. Work includes: intake form spec, risk scoring rubric, lane definitions and SLA targets, runbooks/playbooks per lane, integration with the readiness probe library (network-probe), dashboard telemetry, pilot with 3 customers, and handoff plan to Solutions & Support. Not in scope: changes requiring kernel/runtime-level changes to the serving stack (these remain ENG initiatives).

Success metrics: median first response time <= 2 business days for self-serve lane, <= 5 business days for assisted lane; fraction of requests auto-classified >= 65%; pilot CSAT >= 90%; reduction in escalation-to-engineering by 40% within first quarter post-launch.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form live in Support portal and Console with required fields (network topology sketch, business impact, maintenance window constraints, allowed contacts). 2) Risk scoring rubric implemented as a serverless function that returns lane: self-serve / assisted / escalation. 3) Playbooks and comms templates published (internal Confluence + external-facing KB) for each lane. 4) Dashboard tile in Private Console showing active requests and SLA timers. 5) Pilot completed with 3 customers (one low-risk, one mid-risk, one high-risk) and documented learnings. 6) Security sign-off and runbook for air-gapped approval steps verified. 7) Handoff E2E to Solutions & Support with training session recorded.
